written.headline: ToolSmith auto-generates tools for multimodal search agents
written.summary: Researchers Rui Sun and colleagues introduced ToolSmith, a framework that automatically generates and reuses tool modules for multimodal search agents instead of relying on a hand-crafted library. They report it improves over the base library across three in-domain and ten out-of-domain benchmarks, with larger backbones gaining more.

written.headline: Researchers show physical chip attack can disable AI safety refusals
written.summary: Researchers at Radboud University demonstrated FATCAT, a non-invasive electromagnetic fault-injection attack that forces Llama 3.2 1B and Gemma 3 1B models to comply with restricted requests by corrupting chip-level memory, and showed it can cause a robot arm to make hazardous movements.

written.headline: Virginia and Oregon sue Musk companies over Grok sexualized images
written.summary: Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones and Oregon's attorney general filed separate lawsuits Monday alleging that Musk companies including SpaceX, X, and SpaceXSI stripped industry-standard safeguards from the Grok chatbot to boost users, enabling creation of child sexual abuse material and nonconsensual intimate imagery.

written.headline: Sarvam AI launches Dictate API for English and 22 Indian languages
written.summary: Sarvam AI has released Sarvam Dictate, a speech‑to‑text API that supports English and 22 Indian languages, priced at ₹0.50 per minute. In tests, it required 40% fewer character edits than Gemini 3.5 Transcribe for English and 47% fewer for Indian languages.

written.headline: Nasscom proposes three-year AI scheme for Indian IT firms in Budget 2027-28
written.summary: Nasscom has proposed a three-year AI Services Transformation and Innovation Scheme in its pre-Budget recommendations for 2027-28, to be designed jointly by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology and the Finance Ministry. The scheme would support Indian IT firms in developing and commercialising AI products and services, including through licensing, subscriptions, usage-based payments and outcome-linked arrangements.

written.headline: Mollick: Anthropic paper finds AI value comes from changing org roles
written.summary: Ethan Mollick highlights two findings from a new Anthropic paper: the most AI value comes from changing the organization and roles, and there is wide worker resistance to AI adoption. He suggests changes that expand what workers do and share AI gains with them could help.

written.headline: Systematix report: AI adoption to sustain Indian IT services demand, labor models pressured
written.summary: A Systematix report says growing AI adoption will sustain demand for Indian IT services firms as enterprises need help integrating and deploying AI at scale, even as automation pressures traditional labor-based delivery models.

written.headline: Microsoft builds in-house Rocket system to train AI models at scale
written.summary: Microsoft has developed an in-house reinforcement learning framework called Rocket to train its three-trillion-parameter MAI Base 2 model over weeks or months across thousands of GPUs, reducing dependence on third-party models. The company says its model recently surpassed Claude Opus 4.8 on an aggregate reasoning benchmark and is on track to overtake GPT-5.6 Sol in the coming weeks.
